newsitem.title: GERMANY: Little hope of accord in Lufthansa talks-union.
newsitem.headline: Little hope of accord in Lufthansa talks-union.

text.p: German white collar union DAG said sees little chance of agreement being reached soon in the current round of pay talks for Lufthansa's 50,000 employees, a DAG spokesman told Reuters on Thursday.

Leader of DAG's negotiating team Michael Tarp said the union was looking to break off talks for four weeks to think about how negotiations should continue and to sound out Lufthansa employees on their views.

On Wednesday evening, Lufthansa made a proposal to run over the 27 months to the end of 1998. This includes a 30 percent of base salary one-off payment for the remainder of 1996 and for 1997, followed by a 1.3 percent pay rise in 1998.
The offer also includes 500 marks worth of Lufthansa stock as part of a unique profit-sharing scheme for a German company still partially state-owned.
DAG said the real value of the amounts involved in the airline's offer, and the duration of the payment period, were not acceptable.

The public sector union OeTV, which is simultaneously in negotiations with Lufthansa, said on Wednesday it would discuss the airline's proposals. Traditionally Lufthansa holds separate talks with DAG and OeTV.
OeTV had earlier demanded a 2.3 percent wage rise while DAG was looking for a four percent increase in wages for the 50,000 workers covered by the contract.
